newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault looks to dealers, suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Renault looks to dealers, suppliers.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA is looking to both its dealers and suppliers for help in improving its performance, Chairman Louis Schweitzer said on Thursday.

"We're convinced suppliers can help us, not so much by reducing their (profit) margins -- we can't ask them to do that -- but by helping conceive components with the same properties for less," he told reporters at a briefing on the group's 1996 results.
Officials said that this type of cooperation had saved "hundreds of millions of francs" last year. "In 1996, we did better than we expected, and that can be pursued in 1997," he said.
The company also said in its earnings statement that it would examine the possibility of turning its dealer network into a subsidiary. Renault currently owns some of its dealers.

Schweitzer said such a move would allow for a change in the employees' status -- they currently fall under the metallurgical workers' convention -- and allow the establishment of a profit centre. "Our subsidiaries generate better results than our branches," he added.
